:::{#exm-breusch-pagan-bw}
#### Breusch--Pagan test for the `birthweight` interaction model

For the `birthweight` interaction model (@eq-BW-lm-interact),
$z_i$ holds sex, gestational age, and their interaction,
so $q = 3$.
We fit the auxiliary regression by hand
and compare the result with `lmtest::bptest()`:

```{r}
bp_aux <-
  bw |>
  mutate(resid_sq = resid(bw_lm2)^2) |>
  lm(resid_sq ~ sex + age + sex:age, data = _)

bp_n <- nobs(bw_lm2)
bp_r2 <- summary(bp_aux)$r.squared
bp_stat <- bp_n * bp_r2
bp_p <- pchisq(bp_stat, df = 3, lower.tail = FALSE)

lmtest::bptest(bw_lm2)
```

By @def-breusch-pagan:

$$
\ba
\text{BP}
&= n R^2_{\text{aux}}
&& \text{(studentized statistic)}
\\
&= `r bp_n` \times `r round(bp_r2, 4)`
&& \text{(substitute } n \text{ and } R^2_{\text{aux}}\text{)}
\\
&\approx `r round(bp_stat, 3)`
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

Comparing this value with a $\chi^2_3$ distribution
(@thm-breusch-pagan-null)
gives $p \approx `r round(bp_p, 2)`$,
which matches `bptest()`.
So the test gives no evidence
that the residual variance changes with sex or gestational age.
With only `r bp_n` babies, though,
the test has little power to detect a moderate change.
:::
